item.title: Flarre.AI Launches Insurance AI Platform
item.description: The platform combines an insurance knowledge graph, an agent studio, an orchestration layer and prebuilt point solutions, according to a Flarre.AI statement. “Flarre.AI answers all three by design, in a secure environment with the organization’s context encoded in a knowledge graph.” The company says its platform supports more than 25 lines of business across P&C and life/annuity, including auto, property, specialty lines such as D&O and cyber, life insurance, group benefits, disability and retirement products. (Image source: Flarre.AI.) Flarre.AI (Tampa, Fla.) has launched its agentic AI platform for property/casualty and life/annuity insurers.

item.title: Meta, 29 States Head to Court in Biggest Test Yet of Youth Social Media Litigation
item.description: Related: Appeals Court Allows Thousands of Social Media Suits Over User Addiction Claims to Proceed In terms of potential damages and implications for Meta, the trial is the biggest test yet of youth social media litigation and comes amid a broader reckoning across the globe over social media’s effects on young users. Meta Platforms will face a coalition of state attorneys general in a California federal court trial beginning on Wednesday over claims it engineered Facebook and Instagram to be addictive to children, a case that could expose the company to massive damages and force it to make sweeping changes to its platforms. The trial in Oakland, expected to last seven weeks, will test Colorado, Kentucky, California and New Jersey’s allegations that Meta designed its platforms to keep young users hooked and misled consumers about their safety.

item.title: FlightAware Sues Kalshi Over Flight-Cancellation Markets
item.description: Flight-tracking service FlightAware is suing prediction markets giant Kalshi accusing the company of using its data and name to run “gambling markets on flight cancellations” without permission. (Reporting by Parashuraman in Bengaluru; Editing by Lincoln Feast.) Get the latest insurance news sent straight to your inbox.

item.title: Contiguous U.S. Breaks Record for Hottest Month Ever: NOAA
item.description: The contiguous United States sizzled to its hottest month ever last month, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. The biggest driver of the record heat was nighttime lows that smashed the old record for hottest minimums by 0.7 degrees, NOAA said. The heat was so widespread that every one of the Lower 48 states was at least 1 degree Fahrenheit (nearly 0.6 degrees Celsius) warmer than the 20th-century average, said Russ Vose, chief of monitoring at NOAA’s National Center for Environmental Information.

item.title: Judge Balks at Holding California Utility Liable for Eaton Wildfire
item.description: Insurance companies lost a bid to hold Edison International’s Southern California utility liable for a massive Los Angeles-area wildfire without a trial. If the judge makes her tentative ruling final, Edison will get a chance to argue to a jury at a trial set for next year that the unusual circumstances around the ignition of the Eaton Fire do not qualify for inverse condemnation — the legal principle under which California property owners can recover their losses without having to prove that a utility acted recklessly. Superior Court Judge Laura Seigle on Tuesday tentatively denied a request to hold Southern California Edison on the hook for billions of dollars in property losses under a state law that holds utilities automatically liable when their equipment starts a fire.

item.title: Insurers Overestimate Their Progress With AI: Study
item.description: A study of more than 300 respondents covering several industries finds a considerable disconnect between how organizations assess their progress on AI and where they actually are with real-world AI integration in the insurance sector. Enterprise AI Study found a significant shift from experimentation to enterprise-wide scale in AI. Scaling AI is now a high priority for 96% of insurers, compared to 86% in 2025.

item.title: Global data centre insurance market projected to exceed $24bn by 2030: Allianz Commercial
item.description: The global data centre insurance market is projected to grow from currently around US $11 billion to more than $24 billion by 2030, which comes as the market continues to drive an influx of infrastructure risks and opportunities, according to Allianz Commercial, the commercial insurance business of Allianz Group. There have been comments made by senior industry leaders that capacity may be insufficient to support all the data centre builds expected to come online over the next few years, with the insurance-linked securities market seen as a viable source of incremental reinsurance capacity to support this. Thomas Lillelund, CEO of Allianz Commercial, commented: “AI is turning the latest generation of data centers from a specialist real estate asset into mission-critical infrastructure.” “The scale of investment is extraordinary and, as these centers evolve beyond traditional data storage to high-performance compute demands, success will increasingly depend on resilience: access to power, reliable supply chains, robust construction controls, as well as climate-aware site selection and insurance programs that reflect the true accumulation risk.

item.title: Arch net property cat premiums fell 27% in H1. CEO says more risk ceded to third-party capital
item.description: Chief Financial Officer, also said, “Turning to the reinsurance segment, net premiums written were down 10.4 percent from the same quarter one year ago, reflecting reduced ratings from lower rates and a higher level of retrocession purchases, primarily in the specialty and property catastrophe lines.” In recent months we’ve had more evidence of Arch’s continuing third-party capital partnership initiatives, as well as its appetite for retrocession. Over the first-half of 2026, Bermuda headquartered re/insurer Arch Capital reported a 27% reduction in net property catastrophe reinsurance premiums, while its senior executives noted higher cessions to reinsurance (likely retro) and third-party capital providers. Arch Capital appears to be demonstrating cycle management here, in opting to leverage its diversified platform and access to retrocessional and third-party capital to support a reduction in net property catastrophe premiums at a time when the market has softened.

item.title: Lincoln Financial appoints Adam Cohen as Interim CFO
item.description: Lincoln Financial, a US financial services company specialising in insurance, retirement and wealth management products, has announced the appointment of Adam Cohen, Chief Accounting Officer and Treasurer, as Interim Chief Financial Officer. Lincoln will conduct a comprehensive search process to identify its permanent Chief Financial Officer, including consideration of both internal and external candidates. Cohen joined Lincoln in 2022 as Chief Accounting Officer and assumed responsibility for Treasury in 2024.

item.title: Amynta to acquire agricultural industry specialist MGU Southern States Underwriters
item.description: Insurance services provider Amynta Group has agreed to acquire Southern States Underwriters and SSC Insurance Agency (collectively, Southern States Underwriters), the insurance operations of Southern States Cooperative, Inc. A managing general underwriter (MGU) founded in 1953 and based in Richmond, Virginia, Southern States Underwriters provides commercial property and casualty insurance to meet the specialised needs of suppliers, distributors, and service providers for the agricultural industry. Commenting on the deal, Robert Giammarco, Chairman and CEO of Amynta Group, said: “Southern States Underwriters is a well-established and respected business, dedicated to serving the agribusiness market for over 70 years.

item.title: Norman joins Gallagher Re as Divisional Director within its Facultative team
item.description: Gallagher Re, a global reinsurance brokerage and advisory firm, has announced the appointment of Jenna Norman as Divisional Director, Fac. Norman is joining Gallagher Re from WTW, where she most recently served as Reinsurance Broker within the London Market Retro team. Norman brings extensive expertise in Facultative property broking, specialising in Facultative property broking, working extensively on complex property reinsurance placements for both UK and US clients.

item.title: People Moves: IMA Expands Private Equity and M&A Practice
item.description: IMA Financial Group announced the addition of seven new hires to its Private Equity and M&A Practice. Less than five years after its launch, the Private Equity practice includes 50 associates serving more than 350 private equity sponsors and their portfolio companies, supporting $8.4 billion in annual transaction volume. The practice also includes IMA Diligence Services , IMA’s Chicago-based financial due diligence business, providing financial and lender due diligence and transaction advisory services to private equity firms, commercial lenders and institutional investors.

item.title: Washington University in St. Louis Sued for Retaliation
item.description: Louis is being sued for allegedly violating federal law by firing an employee in retaliation for her opposition to race discrimination and filing a discrimination charge with the U.S. According to the suit, Amega Thaier, who worked as a senior program manager at Washington University’s Alvin J. Siteman Cancer Center, complained to both the university and the EEOC that she was separated from her colleagues because of her race during a mandatory training session provided by the University’s Office of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion.

item.title: Texas Trial Lawyers, Once a Democratic Force, Regain Clout in GOP
item.description: The Texas Trial Lawyers Association, once the de facto war chest of the Texas Democratic Party, sponsored the state GOP convention. It’s his profession: Mizani is a personal injury lawyer, a career path once so closely intertwined with Democratic politics that both were pushed to the sidelines when Republicans gained control in Texas in the early 2000s. “For decades, TLR would blame every problem on trial lawyers in Texas,” said Adam Loewy, a personal injury lawyer and social media political commentator who has recently begun donating heavily to GOP candidates.

item.title: ACORD appoints John Kellington as CEO
item.description: ACORD , the insurance industry’s standards-setting body, has appointed John Kellington as chief executive officer, bringing an experienced insurance technology executive back to the organisation. During his time at Cincinnati Insurance, Kellington applied ACORD’s architecture-led IT model to the insurer’s technology operations. “John’s experience and success in implementing data standards marks him as the most fitting champion to advance ACORD’s mission and help create a more digitally connected and efficient insurance industry,” said ACORD Board Chair Robert Kelly, founder, managing director and CEO of Steadfast Group.

item.title: DogPack partners with Healthy Paws to embed pet insurance in platform
item.description: DogPack has partnered with Healthy Paws , a Chubb company, to bring pet insurance directly into DogPack’s platform as the dog-focused technology company expands into essential services for pet owners. The partnership initially targets users in the United States , who will be able to explore Healthy Paws’ accident and illness coverage for dogs and cats through the DogPack app. Healthy Paws provides pet insurance backed by Chubb, with coverage that allows policyholders to visit any licensed veterinarian without network restrictions.

item.title: Cytix raises $7M to manage security risks from AI-driven software development
item.description: “Existing tools can tell you what vulnerabilities you have, but can’t tell you about the risk.” Cytix’s platform continuously monitors software changes, assesses the security risks they create and determines the appropriate response. The platform sits between software development teams and an organisation’s security, risk and compliance functions, providing a central view of what has changed, the potential business impact and how the resulting risks were handled. Cybersecurity startup Cytix has raised $7 million in Series A funding to scale its change risk management platform as AI-assisted software development accelerates the pace and volume of code changes.

item.title: Salty relaunches as AI-native insurance provider
item.description: Salty founder and CEO James Hall announced the relaunch of the company as an AI-native insurance provider focused on American households with car payments. The new Salty.AI will work on customers’ behalf by finding suitable insurance policies, monitoring rates and coverage, and providing support when claims arise. Founded in 2019, Salty Dot initially offered an embedded insurance platform that allowed consumers to purchase auto insurance during the car-buying process.

item.title: Skan AI raises $63 million
item.description: Skan AI, a startup building the context engine for human and agentic execution, announced $63 million in funding co-led by Cathay Innovation and Dell Technologies Capital, with participation from Citi Ventures, Bloomberg Beta, State Farm Ventures, and Wipro Ventures. Founded in 2018, Skan AI observes how work gets done across every role, system, and application – translating those observations into the execution logic AI needs to perform the work. We think the bigger opportunity is building a better navigation system.” Avinash Misra, Co-founder and CEO of Skan AI.

item.title: OneShield Appoints Rick Becker as Senior Vice President, New Products
item.description: Marlborough, MA — August 7, 2026 – OneShield , a leading provider of core insurance technology solutions for property and casualty insurers and MGAs, has appointed Rick Becker as Senior Vice President, New Products. OneShield is at the cutting edge of the industry’s transformation and has the team, the customer base, and the conviction to help them get there, and that’s why I’m here.” Becker’s appointment reflects OneShield’s continued investment in practical tools its customers can put to work. **************** For more information or to schedule a media interview, please contact: Kaitlyn Jakovcic Senior Product Marketing Manager OneShield kjakovcic@oneshield.com About OneShield OneShield develops and delivers modern, flexible core systems to P&C carriers and MGAs.

item.title: LatAm convierte al pago inmediato en un estándar, pero el desafío es rentabilizar la infraestructura
item.description: La evolución de los pagos inmediatos apunta hacia el desarrollo de una infraestructura capaz de operar a escala y sostenerse económicamente. Ahora que la interoperabilidad y la velocidad son un estándar, los bancos en la región coinciden en que es necesario buscar nuevos verticales de negocios para capitalizar esta normalidad transaccional. “La tecnología, cualquiera que sea, tiene que repercutir o en el servicio a los clientes o en la eficiencia operativa de la institución, y eso es lo que guía el tipo de inversión en tecnología que hacemos”, dijo Ernesto Borbón, director de soluciones de pago en BanBajío, durante el webinar del lanzamiento del I nforme Anual sobre Innovación en Pagos 2026 , elaborado por iupana .

item.title: Underwriting’s Next Job: Governance Steward
item.description: A decade ago, when an underwriter entered an incorrect number or misread a file, the damage was contained to one policy. Today, a single flaw in a model’s logic or a bad software update can repeat the same mistake across thousands of policies before anyone notices. The error moved from the person to the architecture.

item.title: ACORD Names Kellington CEO
item.description: ACORD, the standards-setting body for the insurance industry, announced that it has appointed John Kellington as chief executive officer. While at Cincinnati Insurance, Kellington used the ACORD architecture-led IT model in shaping the insurer’s information technology operations. ACORD said Kellington was instrumental in developing the ACORD Reference Architecture, a series of models representing capabilities, processes, information and components for the insurance industry.

item.title: Sector Snapshot: Fitness Startup Funding Is Rebounding, But Investors Want AI And Data, Not Treadmills
item.description: Venture investors, luckily, seem to be more upbeat than they have been in years about the future of fitness and wellness. Startup investment in those categories totaled more than $3.6 billion in the first half of this year, putting 2026 on pace to come in about a third higher than 2025 , though notably last year marked the lowest sum for wellness-related startup funding in at least six years. For example, connected fitness devices startups Tonal and Hydrow each raised hundreds of millions of dollars during the peak funding years, but haven’t received new investment in three-plus years.

item.title: Exclusive: ClearJet raises $25M to build the ‘Uber of Cargo’
item.description: Rather than build its own fleet of planes or trucks, it connects shippers with unused cargo capacity on commercial flights already traveling between U.S. Instead, its asset-light “Uber for cargo” model taps available capacity on flights that are already traveling between cities. ClearJet , an AI-enabled logistics technology startup, has raised a $25 million Series B, it tells Crunchbase News exclusively.

item.title: Maturing alternative capital partnerships help reinsurers exceed cost of capital: AM Best
item.description: Reinsurers are benefiting from maturing partnerships with alternative capital providers, helping them to consistently exceed their capital costs, a new report from rating agency AM Best has highlighted. For the third consecutive year, global reinsurers have generated returns well above the cost of capital, which AM Best states is due to positive underwriting results that have been driven by repricing and derisking of reinsurance portfolios. According to the agency’s report, the reinsurance industry’s weighted average cost of capital increased to 8.23% in 2025 from 7.67% in 2024, and then rose further again in the first quarter of 2026, to 8.63%.

item.title: Hannover Re still finding growth in property cat, expects price reductions to decelerate: Althoff
item.description: Hannover Re acknowledges reinsurance pricing is declining fastest in property catastrophe risks, but the company continues to find some growth opportunities here and expects price reductions will begin to decelerate now that rates have come down for two consecutive years, Sven Althoff said today. Property cat is the area where we see most softening, and then many other parts of our portfolio are significantly more stable when it comes to the terms and conditions.” Moving on to discuss natural catastrophe reinsurance business, Althoff said that growth opportunities are still being found. Althoff, Hannover Re’s Executive Board Member for Property & Casualty business, also highlighted that capital over-supply in property catastrophe reinsurance remains largely constrained to the higher-layers of towers, where appetites are strongest.

item.title: BSX streamlines listings for previously approved insurance-linked securities (ILS) programmes
item.description: The Bermuda Stock Exchange (BSX) continues to optimise its process for listing new insurance-linked securities (ILS), with a streamlining announced that will allow for guaranteed next day listings, with same day possible in certain cases, for previously approved insurance-linked securities (ILS) programmes. The move streamlines the process for listing new insurance-linked securities (ILS) issued under previously approved ILS programmes, with guaranteed next business day listing approval and a chance of same day in some cases, as long as relevant documentation is submitted in time and good order. Recall that, the Bermuda Stock Exchange (BSX) remains the main venue for listings of catastrophe bonds and other insurance-linked securities (ILS).

item.title: Data centre insurance market forecast to exceed $24bn by 2030: Allianz
item.description: The global data centre insurance market is forecast to more than double to over USD $24 billion by 2030, as the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence infrastructure increases the value, complexity and concentration of risks faced by insurers, according to Allianz Commercial, the commercial insurance business of Allianz Group. Allianz Commercial estimates that the market will increase from around USD $11 billion currently to more than USD $24 billion by 2030. Indeed, comprehensive insurance cover has become a prerequisite for financing many large-scale AI infrastructure projects.” According to Allianz Commercial, the changing scale of data centres is also increasing the potential severity of insurance losses.

item.title: Waters to lead AXA XL’s Large Commercial and Specialty business unit
item.description: AXA XL, the property and casualty specialty risk division of AXA, has announced the appointment of Matt Waters as Head of its Large Commercial and Specialty business unit, effective immediately. In his new role, Waters will be responsible for leading AXA XL’s Large Commercial and Specialty lines portfolio across the US, Canada, and Bermuda. “He’s excited to leverage our talented Large Commercial and Specialty underwriting teams to support consistent disciplined underwriting and deliver valuable solutions to our clients and broker partners.” Jim DiVirgilio, AXA XL’s recently retired Chief Claims Officer who is now serving in an advisory role, is stepping in to temporarily lead the Mid-Market team while a search for new leadership is conducted.

item.title: AM Best maintains stable outlook for GCC insurance markets
item.description: AM Best is maintaining its stable outlook for the insurance markets of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC). Other positive factors supporting AM Best’s segment outlook include opportunities for insurance sector growth, as increasing insurable risks remain an important feature of the market. AM Best highlighted the segment’s reliance on reinsurance, primarily to support specialty, commercial property and engineering lines of business.

item.title: Putin Threatens Retaliation Over EU Moves to Seize Russian Ships
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin threatened to retaliate against any European Union moves to seize his country’s commercial ships, calling such actions “piracy.” As part of a new sanctions package last month, the bloc approved a mechanism allowing member states to sell oil and other goods seized from sanctioned vessels detained at sea. “We see that the authorities of some countries, in violation of international maritime law, are trying to restrict the movement of ships,” Putin said Wednesday during Pacific Fleet exercises in Russia’s Far East. Of course, this is nothing other than piracy and robbery.” Read more: Oman Says Spill From Grounded Shadow Oil Tanker Covers 400 Square Kilometers Putin said Russia would respond in kind, and not necessarily in the same waters where Russian vessels could be targeted but anywhere “we ourselves consider it necessary and appropriate.” The US, the UK and the EU have sanctioned hundreds of tankers for helping Russia export oil to fund the Kremlin’s war on Ukraine.

item.title: OSHA Fines Maine Pulp Mill $700K for Chemical Release That Killed 2 Workers
item.description: A federal investigation into the release of a deadly gas at a Baileyville-based wood pulp mill found that the employer exposed workers to safety and health hazards that resulted in the death of two workers. OSHA said it also investigated a March 7, 2026, chemical fire at Woodland Pulp that started after the employer released 4,400 gallons of 50 percent hydrogen peroxide that mixed with wood pulp accumulated on the ground. According to OSHA, Woodland Pulp has been inspected 13 times since 2017 resulting in 13 serious and one other-than-serious citation, including an inspection started in 2017 when 14 employees were taken to the hospital after a chemical exposure in the same area covered by the current inspections.

item.title: People Moves: World Insurance Names CFO, World Retail
item.description: World Insurance Associates Names Casey CFO World Insurance Associates LLC , headquartered in Iselin, New Jersey, named Ann Casey as World Retail chief financial officer effective September 1. Casey will lead the retail controllership and retail M&A accounting integration functions and will partner with World’s retail division and practice leaders on strategy, process improvement, and financial performance across the organization. Casey joined World in 2024 as head of retail premium accounting.

item.title: Insurance Intake Gets a Branding Layer, as Canopy Connect Introduces Trailhead
item.description: Canopy Connect believes that a big chunk of that leak is fixable with branding and modern sharing mechanics. “Your intake link is often the first thing a prospect sees from you,” said Tolga Tezel, Canopy Connect’s founder and CEO . Canopy Connect argues that a partner can now forward an agent’s Trailhead link as-is and have it carry the introduction on its own.

item.title: Lecturas, podcasts e inspiración para un verano con propósito
item.description: El verano regala algo que durante el resto del año escasea: tiempo para detenernos, reflexionar y descubrir nuevas ideas. Aunque la desconexión no siempre es la deseada. Desde #RedEWI creemos que el liderazgo también se cultiva lejos de las reuniones, los informes y la agenda diaria.

item.description: Insurance companies lost a bid to hold Edison International’s Southern California utility liable for a massive Los Angeles-area wildfire without a trial. Superior Court Judge Laura Seigle on Tuesday tentatively denied a request to put Southern California Edison on the hook for billions of dollars in property losses under a state law that holds utilities automatically liable when their equipment starts a fire. Related: Edison Says Its Equipment Likely Associated With 2025 LA Fire If the judge makes her tentative ruling final, Edison will get a chance to argue to a jury at a trial set for next year that the unusual circumstances around the ignition of the Eaton Fire do not qualify for inverse condemnation — the legal principle under which California property owners can recover their losses without having to prove that a utility acted recklessly.

item.title: GM Sets Up $4.5 Billion Plan to Ensure Supply of Critical Parts
item.description: has set a plan to guarantee the supply of as much as $4.5 billion in critical auto parts to safeguard the company from supply shocks caused by such events as extreme weather, natural disasters and cyberattacks. The automaker reached a deal with Procura Auto Parts LLC, which will buy parts inventory from key suppliers and front the cash, GM said in a securities filing on Tuesday. The automaker will pay Procura interest and fees upfront, and pay for the parts when it needs them.

item.title: ‘Guac Signal’ Sparked Chipotle’s Frantic Bid to Recall Jalapeños
item.description: figured out it was the jalapeños, its automated recall system began calling restaurants, again and again and again. They’d sent the company a “guac signal,” warning there was trouble with something in the guacamole. But it was Chipotle that narrowed it down to the jalapeños first — days before authorities announced nationwide recalls last week.

item.title: Hannover Re H1 income +7%, volumes up amid price declines. Only shares EUR 18m losses with ILS
item.description: Hannover Re has reported 7% higher first-half net income of EUR 1.4 billion for the first-half of 2026, while the reinsurance firm reported higher underwriting volumes at mid-year renewals amid continued price declines. Property and casualty reinsurance volumes were affected by the ongoing price declines being seen in the softening market environment. Net new business contract service margin came down 13.3% to EUR 1.7 billion, which Hannover Re noted was “driven primarily by price declines in the most recent rounds of renewals as well as exchange rate effects, partially offset by volume growth due to increased new business – especially in the second quarter.” Gross reinsurance revenue in P&C risks fell by 8.0% to EUR 8.8 billion, or 3.9% at unchanged exchange rates.

item.title: Rokstone expands Athena Cyber proposition with supply chain cover
item.description: Rokstone, the international specialty re/insurance MGA, has expanded its Athena Cyber proposition with a new extension designed to provide cover for supply chain disruption caused by cyber incidents involving an insured’s customers or suppliers. Rokstone said the cover differs from traditional contingency business interruption insurance by specifically addressing cyber-related disruption across an insured’s wider commercial network. Research cited by Rokstone indicates that 61% of organisations have experienced a supply chain breach, while almost a third of affected organisations have experienced operational disruption, financial losses or regulatory fines.

item.title: RT Specialty promotes Provenzo to Director, London Markets & Delegated Authority
item.description: RT Specialty , a wholesale distributor of specialty insurance products and services and the wholesale broking specialty of Ryan Specialty, has promoted Greg Provenzo to Director, London Markets & Delegated Authority. In his new position, and as part of the RT Binding Authority leadership team, Provenzo will provide strategic leadership and operational oversight for RT Binding Authority’s London Markets commercial business. He will focus on driving profitable growth by managing Syndicate and carrier relationships, refining underwriting strategies, and guiding delegated authority portfolios, while serving as a primary bridge between production teams and London markets.

item.title: Hannover Re delivers net income rise of 7% to €1.4bn as P&C combined ratio strengthens
item.description: Global reinsurer Hannover Re saw its Group net income rise from $1.3 billion last year to $1.4 billion in the first half of 2026, as operating profit increased by almost 10% to €1.9 billion, with an improved property and casualty (P&C) combined ratio of 83.2%. Hannover Re says that it delivered a “very good half-year result in an increasingly challenging market landscape”, and is confident of still being on track to meet its full year 2026 earnings guidance of at least €2.7 billion. This year, Hannover Re grew its book by 12.3% to a volume of €4.24 billion, although prices on the renewed business retreated by 4.5% on an inflation and risk-adjusted basis.

item.title: Rhine River Shipping Stalls as Water Level Hits Record Low
item.description: Water levels on the Rhine river are dwindling further, with no relief in sight, forcing companies that rely on the waterway to adjust rapidly to keep goods flowing.Levels at Kaub, Germany — the Rhine’s shallowest point — have fallen to the lowest since records began in 1880, and could drop further as another heat wave bakes Europe this week. “The Rhine’s low water levels are restricting inland shipping capacities and posing major challenges for logistics and supply chains,” chemicals firm Evonik Industries AG said Tuesday. The company is reacting “with extensive precautionary measures and is shifting a part of its freight transport to rail and road.” Like Evonik, BASF reported isolated bottlenecks, but said it’s been able to keep shipping along the river by deploying more vessels designed for low-water conditions.

item.title: Americans Just Endured the Hottest Month in 132 Years
item.description: The US just sweltered through the warmest month ever recorded. “In a few years, this will feel like a cool July.” The July record is the result of weeks of scorching temperatures in the US, including a heat dome over the July 4 holiday and sweeping heat warnings later that month. The US government has been tracking temperatures for 132 years.
